assessments.support: The publicly available data set comprises data from 48 people with ASD and 65 TCs, with no signiﬁcant diﬀerences in demographics between the two groups. TCs were excluded for those who received a score of 10 or higher on the Social Communication Questionnaire 14 or a score of 6 or higher on the Obsessive/Compulsive subscale of the Spence Children’s Anxiety Scale (SCAS) 16.
The data set was collected at the University of Michigan, one of the ABIDE data collection sites Age, sex and IQ comparisons reported with no significant group differences.
we performed preprocessing based on the Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (C-PAC, http://fcp-indi.github.io). The images were slice-time and motion corrected.
Relies on the ABIDE site's own ASD diagnosis; TC inclusion/exclusion criteria (SCQ, SCAS) described, but ASD diagnostic instrument not specified in this paper.
Age and sex compared between groups (Wilcoxon, chi-square) with no significant difference; single-site design removes between-site variance but limits generalisability.
Six motion parameters, WM and CSF signals regressed; no explicit motion-threshold exclusion rule or ComBat (single site, so site handling not applicable).
Pearson correlation functional connectivity between AAL ROIs, Fisher Z-transformed, a standard approach.

We further validate the detected subnetwork features by performing classiﬁcation analysis. We employ the support vector machine with radial basis function kernel and linear kernel as our classiﬁer. The classification features (detected abnormal subnetworks) were identified using the full case-control sample before being validated with leave-one-out cross-validation, risking optimistic performance estimates from feature-selection leakage.

risk_of_bias.summary: Well-described single-site ABIDE cohort and C-PAC/AAL pipeline, but the subnetwork features used for LOOCV classification were derived from network-detection analysis of the full sample rather than from training folds only, a feature-selection leakage risk; single-site design also limits site generalisability (acknowledged by the authors).

charting.title: Latent and Abnormal Functional Connectivity Circuits in Autism Spectrum Disorder
charting.primary_goal: Apply a novel statistical network-detection method to identify latent and abnormal functional connectivity circuits distinguishing ASD from typical controls in single-site ABIDE resting-state fMRI data.
charting.study_setting: Single site (University of Michigan, ABIDE I)
charting.healthy_status_confirmed: TCs were excluded for those who received a score of 10 or higher on the Social Communication Questionnaire 14 or a score of 6 or higher on the Obsessive/Compulsive subscale of the Spence Children’s Anxiety Scale (SCAS) 16.
charting.age_matched: No significant difference (Wilcoxon rank sum, p>0.05)
charting.neurodevelopmentally_typical: Typical controls (TCs) were included by the criteria that either verbal or non-verbal IQ was ≥85 and were aged at least 7 years
charting.sensitive_data_anonymized: Yes (HIPAA identifiers and facial information removed per ABIDE release process)
charting.feature_types: Pairwise functional connectivity (Pearson correlation, Fisher Z) between AAL ROIs
charting.specific_features: Correlation matrix over the first 90 AAL regions; latent/abnormal subnetworks identified by a novel statistical graph detection algorithm
charting.importance_method: Novel network-detection/testing algorithm identifying differentially-expressed edges/subnetworks
charting.top_features_identified: Two abnormal connectivity subnetworks, one overlapping left middle temporal gyrus/precuneus; second showing k-partite topology linked to emotion/empathy regions
charting.specific_algorithms: SVM (RBF and linear kernels) classification using detected subnetwork features
charting.key_performance_results: The leave-one-out cross-validation results show that the accuracy rates are 89 and 84% correspondingly.
charting.summary_key_findings: A novel network-detection method identified latent and abnormal ASD-related functional connectivity subnetworks (involving middle temporal gyrus/precuneus and emotion/empathy-related regions) in single-site ABIDE data; SVM classification using these subnetwork features achieved 89% (RBF) and 84% (linear kernel) leave-one-out cross-validated accuracy.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Abnormal connectivity subnetworks involving left middle temporal gyrus, precuneus, and regions implicated in emotion/empathy processing
charting.future_directions_recommended: we only utilize a subset of ABIDE data base, and we plan to compare results from diﬀerent study sites and perform meta-analysis in future work.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Both associational (network detection) and predictive (SVM validation); single-site ABIDE I (University of Michigan), 48 ASD / 65 TC
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC preprocessing, AAL atlas (90 ROIs), Pearson correlation + Fisher Z functional connectivity, a novel statistical graph network-detection/testing algorithm to identify abnormal subnetworks, SVM (RBF/linear) leave-one-out cross-validation using the detected subnetwork features.
narrative_row.outcomes: Two abnormal connectivity subnetworks identified (middle temporal gyrus/precuneus; emotion/empathy-linked k-partite network); SVM classification using these features achieved 89% (RBF) and 84% (linear) leave-one-out accuracy.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Single ABIDE site only (acknowledged by authors as future work to extend to multiple sites/meta-analysis); classification features derived from full-sample network detection prior to cross-validation, risking leakage; no numeric motion-QC threshold reported.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a novel subnetwork-detection method on a well-characterised single ABIDE site, illustrating both an associational discovery step and a predictive validation step, useful as a methodological contrast to multi-site ABIDE classification studies.
